item.title: RJ Luis Jr. reportedly will sue SEC, Greg Sankey for violating injunction that made him eligible at LSU
item.description: RJ Luis Jr. recorded 11 points and nine rebounds in his lone game for LSU this season, a 79-67 win over Louisiana-Monroe on Nov. 18. AP Photo/Ella Hall RJ Luis Jr. will sue the SEC and its commissioner, Greg Sankey, for violating the preliminary injunction that made him eligible at LSU, Luis’ attorney, Tony Clayton, told ESPN on Monday night. Luis, a former St. John’s star who saw NBA preseason action after going undrafted last year, is seeking “a large number” in damages, Clayton reportedly said. Clayton, per ESPN’s report, is planning on deposing every SEC president. Searching for evidence that Sankey strung together a league-wide boycott of LSU after head men’s basketball coach Will Wade played Luis last week, Clayton reportedly said he’s already sent “preservation” letters. ESPN’s report about Luis’ imminent lawsuit against the SEC and Sankey arrived on the same day the SEC announced that it filed an amended complaint and a motion for a temporary restraining order in its federal lawsuit against LSU . And, in a four-page declaration that was part of Monday’s court filing, Sankey revealed that the conference intends to hold a special meeting of presidents on Dec. 3 to determine whether LSU should be expelled from the league . RJ Luis Jr. earned Big East Player of the Year honors in 2024-25 while averaging 18.2 points per game for St. John's. ASSOCIATED PRESS This isn’t the first time expulsion threats have surrounded LSU. Those previously surfaced when Tigers head football coach Lane Kiffin seriously contemplated rostering players who had previously signed contracts with NFL teams. This all stems from an eligibility crisis that resulted from the NCAA adopting its five-for-five model . In attempt to streamline eligibility rules, the organization rolled out an age-based system to replace a format that allowed four seasons of competition over five years with no age restrictions. The five-for-five model, however, excluded athletes who used their final year of eligibility during the 2025-26 academic year, many of whom graduated high school in 2022. In turn, a collection of athletes from the 2022 high school class have fought legally to benefit from a fifth year as well. That group includes Luis , who played one season at UMass prior to spending two more at St. John’s and then declaring for the 2025 NBA Draft. At the time, Luis was the reigning Big East Player of the Year. Even so, he went undrafted. Luis still wound up inking a two-way contract with the Utah Jazz and playing in NBA preseason games for the Boston Celtics. Then, flash forward to this month, when he received his newest preliminary injunction, which paved the way for him to suit up for LSU against Louisiana-Monroe last Wednesday. A Louisiana judge ruled that the SEC and NCAA couldn’t penalize LSU for playing Luis. item.title: Chelsea star reveals he almost retired after serious injury issues
item.description: Chelsea star reveals he almost retired after serious injury issues Wesley Fofana Opens Up on Chelsea Injury Hell and Retirement Thoughts Wesley Fofana has said he came close to walking away from football during a brutal spell of injuries at Chelsea. It is a stark admission, and it tells you plenty about the mental toll long-term setbacks can take on a player, especially one still only 25. The Chelsea defender has been under pressure again this season after a run of poor displays under Xabi Alonso, including the 4-1 home defeat to Leeds. That is the easy part for the outside world to judge. The harder part is what sits underneath it, the grind of recovery, the fear of the next setback, and the feeling that your body is no longer reliable. Injury Struggles Pushed Fofana to Edge Fofana explained how the lowest point came after a series of serious physical problems. “There was a period when I was recovering from my cruciate ligament and meniscus injuries,” Fofana said. He then added, “Then I suffered two consecutive hamstring strains under Enzo Maresca, when I really decided: ‘That’s it, I’m retiring, I’m done playing.’ I was serious.” That is not throwaway language. Players say many things in frustration, but this sounds considered, direct and real. Fofana described a period where football had become almost entirely associated with pain. “I really wanted to stop, because, for the first time in my life, I wasn’t happy anymore. It wasn’t just about being injured or not playing; my whole life was completely shattered. I wasn’t myself anymore. I sincerely believed that, in the future, I would only get injured.” Photo IMAGO Chelsea Defender Faced Psychological Battle The most revealing part of Fofana’s account is how quickly self-doubt took hold. “I thought to myself: ‘That’s it, football isn’t for me, I’m too fragile.’ I even used Abou Diaby as an example. I thought to myself: ’I guess I’m the Abou Diaby of our generation. There has to be someone like that, and it happened to me. It’s my destiny, I accept it.’” That is the voice of a player who had stopped trusting his own future. Injuries damage muscles and ligaments, but they also shred confidence. For defenders, where timing, aggression and conviction matter, that cost is huge. Retirement Decision Was Seriously Considered Fofana even contacted his representatives to discuss ending his career. “Of course, I was very sad and didn’t want to stop, because I was living my dream. At that point, I called my agents so we could sit down and talk, telling them, ‘Okay, I’ve decided to retire.’” He went on, “They started analysing the situation with me, talking about contracts and all that: ‘It’s simple, you still have several years left on your contract, and there’s a lot of money to be made. item.title: Scott Hanson points out NFL Week 11 anomaly that ‘hasn’t happened in more than a quarter-century’
item.description: Photo by Carlos Avila Gonzalez/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images Scott Hanson highlighted a remarkable NFL statistic after home teams enjoyed an almost perfect Week 11 in the 2026 season. Six teams had a bye in Week 11, leaving 13 games to be played across the league. The home team won 12 of those 13 games, marking the first time the record had been achieved in 28 years. The last time home teams went 12-1 in a single week was Week 7 of the 1998 season, making this a particularly rare achievement. The only home defeat came at SoFi Stadium, where the Los Angeles Chargers lost 27-24 to the New York Jets . That result meant the Jets became the only visiting team to win during an extraordinary weekend. Interestingly, there was a remarkable coincidence when looking back at the previous 12-1 record in 1998. The Jets were also responsible for the only away victory that week, beating the New England Patriots 24-14. Some fans have pointed out that the San Francisco 49ers’ victory over the Minnesota Vikings also contributed to the latest record. The 49ers defeated the Vikings 35-10 in Mexico City , but were officially designated the home team for the international fixture, so the result counted towards the 12-1 tally. item.title: Sheehan out of Wallabies Test after two-game ban
item.description: Dan Sheehan has 43 caps for Ireland [Getty Images] Ireland's stand-in captain Dan Sheehan has been banned for two games after a croc-roll tackle against South Africa and will play no part against Australia on Friday night. The Leinster forward was shown a yellow card by referee Christophe Ridley in the 72nd minute of Ireland's 20-17 victory over the Springboks in Dublin on Saturday. That was later upgraded to a red card by the foul play review officer (FPRO) on the basis of World Rugby's Law 9.20d that "a player may remove the jackler from the tackle area by pushing/driving them backwards (including by grabbing the knee/leg), but must not roll, pull or twist an opponent". The 28-year-old faced a disciplinary hearing on Monday evening where the panel found that the incident was a "low-entry point" offence and merited a two-week ban. Sheehan will miss Friday's Nations Championship finals weekend fixture against Australia in Twickenham (20:10 GMT) and Leinster's game against Ospreys in the United Rugby Championship (URC) on 4 December. Sheehan played at number eight against South Africa, the first time he has started at the position in his Test career. More usually a hooker, his absence requires another change for Ireland at the base of the scrum for what is their final game of 2026. South Africa win 'sets us up nicely' - Farrell Did Springboks win change the narrative for Ireland? Ireland remind themselves that the best are beatable Captain Caelan Doris and two-tour British and Irish Lion Jack Conan have missed the entire northern series of the Nations Championship through injury. Connacht's Sean Jansen deputised in the first game of the November slate against Argentina but a knee injury ruled him out for the remainder of the autumn. Nick Timoney moved from open-side flanker for the Fiji game before Sheehan was selected to face the back-to-back world champions. Ireland have an otherwise full squad to choose from for the Wallabies game with head coach Andy Farrell to confirm his selection on Wednesday afternoon (16:00 GMT). "That was a physical affair, as we knew it was going to be," said assistant coach Andrew Goodman of the victory over South Africa. "Plenty of excitement and again, looking forward to a massive opportunity for the squad this week. We've got a full squad of fit bodies, which is great." item.title: Dodgers expected to make one specific roster move after losing Tarik Skubal to Mets
item.description: Dodgers expected to make one specific roster move after losing Tarik Skubal to Mets originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Dodgers are heading into the 2026-2027 MLB offseason in pretty good shape overall. But the most notable roster move has already happened, and they didn't benefit from it. Tarik Skubal, after joining the Dodgers mid-season in a trade from the Detroit Tigers , is reportedly signing with the New York Mets at a whopping $450 million over nine years. The Dodgers just lost their top free agent, albeit without making a competitive offer. But what's next for Los Angeles? Well, according to USA Today's Bob Nightengale , the Dodgers are expected to make one roster move this offseason following Skubal's departure: signing a new starting pitcher. Dodgers plans after losing Tarik Skubal to Mets revealed "The Mets ruined their biggest offseason prize. They aren't going to just sit back and let everyone else ruin their winter," Nightengale writes. "They will sign another free-agent starter." After losing Skubal to the Mets on a massive record-breaking deal, the Dodgers are expected to make an addition to their starting rotation. Yoshinobu Yamamoto leads the starters, with Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, and Emmet Sheehan rounding out the five-man rotation. Shohei Ohtani , if healthy, could be involved as well. This is already a very strong rotation, and it doesn't actually need another addition. But with Skubal gone, the Dodgers could use one more starting pitching option at the big league level for the 2027 season. The best free-agent starters available heading into Thanksgiving are Kevin Gausman, Michael King, Matthew Boyd, Nick Pivetta, Nick Martinez, Casey Mize, Tyler Mahle, Davis Peterson, Clay Holmes, and Robbie Ray, among many others. There are a lot of options to choose from, and Nightengale is fully expecting the Dodgers to add a starter at some point this offseason. It's not a pressing need, but considering the injury history of the Dodgers' starters, adding one more MLB-caliber starter this offseason would make perfect sense. item.title: Jannik Sinner undergoes knee surgery leaving Australian Open participation in doubt
item.description: Jannik Sinner has undergone knee surgery and is now likely to miss the Australian Open in January. The five-time grand slam champion has not played since winning Wimbledon in July and announced he would be ending his season in October. The 25-year-old had planned to return in late December, ahead of the 2027 season, but it was decided that surgery was required to address the issue. According to reports in Italy, Sinner could be sidelined for up to three months after undergoing an operation on the iliotibial band (IT band) in his right leg, although he did not specify a timeline for his recovery when announcing the news. The world No 2 posted on X on Tuesday: “Over the past few months, together with my team we’ve tried everything to treat my injury without surgery. “After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn’t respond as we’d all hoped, that’s why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band. “I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team. Thank you for all your support. See you soon!” Italian outlet Corriere dello Sport reported on Monday that Sinner had travelled to ⁠Turku, Finland to undergo surgery, with his team confirming that the operation was performed by Turku-based orthopaedic surgeon Lasse Lempainen. Despite only playing for half the season Sinner still racked up six titles and a 44-3 win-loss record, and finishes the year ranked second in the world. He successfully defended his Wimbledon title and won five consecutive Masters 1000 crowns, becoming just the second player and the youngest to complete the set of all nine Masters titles over the course of his career.

item.title: Giants might lose up-and-coming coach to fascinating opportunity
item.description: Dennard Wilson has mostly done an excellent job in his first season as the Giants ’ defensive coordinator. So will he become a head coach for the first time in 2027? Maybe. And that opportunity could come at the college level. Wilson recently interviewed via video chat for Maryland’s vacancy, according to NFL Network. Wilson, 44, is from Maryland and played defensive back for the Terrapins from 2000-03. So this would be a homecoming opportunity for him. He played his high school ball at powerhouse DeMatha Catholic. The Giants’ defense just did an excellent job against the Jaguars in Sunday’s 23-18 victory , which moved coach John Harbaugh’s team to 6-3-1. These Giants can smell the NFC East title now. But if Wilson gets the Maryland job, he might have to leave East Rutherford during the season, to begin recruiting efforts. Such is the potential cost of having (and thriving with) a young, up-and-coming assistant like Wilson. “He’s not going to leave the Giants to go in the middle of the season to take the Maryland job,” Harbaugh said. “I don’t know if he’ll take the job or not. We’re getting ahead of ourselves a little bit, I would say. We’ll cross that bridge when we get there. How about that?” Harbaugh said that even if Wilson does get that job, he has “no level of concern that it would interrupt our season at all — none.” Wilson’s unit is currently 10th in Pro Football Focus’ defensive ratings. And he has done that, for the most part, without critically important starters Brian Burns and Tremaine Edmunds, both out for the season. Last season, the Giants finished 23rd in PFF’s defensive ratings. So Wilson has done a transformative job in his first year in East Rutherford. Will it be his only year? Perhaps. Even if Wilson doesn’t get (or want) the Maryland job, he could be in the mix for NFL head coaching opportunities next offseason. It ultimately would not be a stunner at all if Wilson isn’t back with the Giants in 2027. Wilson was the Titans’ defensive coordinator from 2024-25. (AP Photo/Matt Durisko) Matt Durisko The Pro Football Hall of Fame is starting to consider its next batch of infamous players who will be inducted in the Class of 2027. On Tuesday, 52 players (20 offensive and 22 defensive) advanced in the voting process, including six Pittsburgh Steelers. It’s the first year of eligibility for quarterback Ben Roethlisberger and wide receiver Antonio Brown. Roethlisberger was the Steelers’ first-round pick in the 2004 Draft. He wore Black and Gold for 18 seasons and became the youngest quarterback ever to win a Super Bowl. He holds numerous team records and was selected to the Pro Bowl nine times. Brown played with the Steelers from 2010-2018. He finished his 12-season NFL career with 928 receptions for 12,291 yards and 83 receiving touchdowns in 146 regular-season games. The other four former Steelers nominees have repeatedly been up for induction: receiver Hines Ward, linebacker James Harrison, center Maurkice Pouncey and defensive end L.C. Greenwood. The Selection Committee will reduce the current list down to 25 players in about two weeks. Eventually, just 15 candidates will be presented at the Selection Committee’s annual meeting ahead of Super Bowl LXI: 13 players, one coach (Bill Bellickick) and one contributor (Robert Kraft). item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
